input: grid is an n by n binary integer matrix with distinct mutable row objects; empty input is accepted. Zero is water and one is land, and n*n fits shared collection bounds. All collections are ordinary finite dense arrays/lists, not subclasses, proxies, sparse arrays or accessor-backed collections. Node fields, where present, are ordinary data fields. Every individual collection length and computed allocation dimension/count fits [0,4294967295]; explicitly stated padded sizes and heap child-index arithmetic must also fit the declared exact numeric domain. No concurrent mutation or built-in monkey-patching is permitted. Preconditions are not runtime-checked; allocation/resource capacity and actual completion still require qualification. Python integer inputs are plain int excluding bool; any separately declared floating probabilities are ordinary float.
return: Maximum over original water cells of their Manhattan distance to the nearest original land cell, or -1 if no water or no land exists (including empty input).
mutation_aliasing: Intentionally marks each discovered water cell as one before enqueueing. On mixed land/water input every cell ends as one; on empty/all-land/all-water input no writes occur. Outer and row identities/lengths remain unchanged and caller aliases observe writes. Distinct rows are required. No grid is returned; the Solution instance retains no state.
numeric: Distances are at most 2*(n-1), and queue/cell counts at most n*n. Multi-source seeds are exactly original land cells at distance zero; marking on enqueue ensures every original water cell is discovered once. All integer inputs and integer intermediates (apart from opaque Python identity keys) remain in [-9007199254740991,9007199254740991]; no bitwise coercion is used.
complexity: O(n^2 + 1) time and O(n^2 + 1) auxiliary space, counting the retained-head queue and all coordinate/distance triples. No separate visited matrix or recursion. Bounds count ordinary built-in allocations and assume bounded-word arithmetic, constant-time indexing, amortized append/pop, and stated hash/sort guarantees where relevant.
